ria: quick heads-up — I noticed a weird shape in the warmup latency vs prefix-cache hit-rate plot this morning. hit-rate climbs ~60% then p95 latency jumps. attaching profiling notes.
sam: looks familiar. kernel selection seems to flip when the effective hit window crosses ~65% (weird). i pulled a pprof; most time is spent in kv lookup + a kernel path that looks like a recompile/selection. will paste the query i used below.
sam: ```sql
-- compute hit-rate buckets and p95 latency per bucket
SELECT
  floor(hit_rate*100/5)*5 as hit_bucket,
  approx_percentile(latency_ms, 0.95) as p95_ms,
  count(*) as calls,
  any(kernel_variant) as kernel_variant_example
FROM inference.rpc_events
WHERE ts >= now() - interval '6 hours'
  AND route IS NOT NULL
  AND kv_age_seconds < 300 -- ignore stale hits
GROUP BY hit_bucket
ORDER BY hit_bucket
```
andre: fwiw, i think batching heuristics are involved. when hit-rate increases, effective prefix sizes shrink and the batcher sometimes switches from short-window batching (latency-optimized) to larger window batches to improve utilization — that can increase tail latency for first tokens. add kernel_variant and batch_wait_ms to panels.
mel: customer slice backs this up. two tenants had high hit-rate but also very long single-turn prompts (session_length > 1k tokens). warmup tries to prefetch KV but kernel selection produces a slower path for long sequences (cache warms but kernel path slower). also saw increased context-switch counts in the profile.
jordan: suggestion: dashboard idea -> x axis = hit-rate, y axis = p95 latency, split series by kernel_variant and session_length_bin. show per-route and per-customer overlays so we can see if a particular tenant drives the spike. add a tokens_saved_per_call metric and cumulative tokens_saved for dollar impact.

ria: good catches. i'll open a dashboard PR with the per-route/p95-by-hitbucket panels and add kernel_variant + batch_wait_ms labels. also adding tokens_saved and tokens_saved_dollars.
sam: small note: query needs that `kv_age_seconds < 300` filter (otherwise stale hits skew the hitrate shape). also consider excluding synthetic warmup calls where user_id = 'system_warmup'.
andre: added a quick mockup in Miro: https://miro.com/app/board/warmup-hitcurve-mockup (shows kernel_variant stacked lines).
mel: can we add a sampling panel that shows full-session-distribution (session_length histogram) per-tenant? i think the long-tail is key.
ria: action items: 1) dashboard PR with per-route/per-customer hitcurve + kernel/batch labels (i'll take this) 2) synthetic test that mirrors customer session-length distribution (sam + me) 3) alert rule: if hit-rate > 50% and p95 rises >20% vs 24h baseline (jordan will own) 4) bisect commit abc123 and confirm regression source (jordan)
jordan: i'll start bisect and own the alert. ping me when the PR is up and i'll attach the alert policy.
sam: also add a nightly regression check that compares tokens_saved_per_minute to baseline — a drop could indicate a caching keying regression.
ria: thanks all. i'll open the PR and tag @jordan @sam. linking the profiling snapshot in the ticket: https://src.redwood/tickets/INF-4022. will follow up with panel ids once created. :thumbsup:
mel: thanks! once dashboards are live we should run the warmup-hitcurve job in canary for 24h and watch the per-tenant waterfalls.
andre: one final thought — consider exposing `batch_wait_ms` and `kernel_decision_reason` as labels on the metric stream; that will make root-cause much faster.
ria: noted. adding to PR description and runbook. closing this thread for now, continuing in PR comments.
